Natural_Language: This part provides contract modification standards for the workforce to limit risk to the public and government. This part applies to all types of contracts including construction and architect-engineer contracts. This part does not apply to modifications for extraordinary contractual relief (see subpart 50.1).
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_100_a: Part 43 provides contract modification standards for the workforce to limit risk to the public and government; P_43_100_b: Part 43 applies to all types of contracts including construction and architect-engineer contracts; P_43_100_c: Part 43 does not apply to modifications for extraordinary contractual relief
Validation_Notes: Scope provision establishes applicability (conjunction of coverage) with an exclusion for extraordinary contractual relief under subpart 50.1. The negation captures the carve-out. External dependency on Part 50.

Natural_Language: As used in this part - Administrative change means a unilateral (see 43.203(b)) contract change, in writing, that does not affect the substantive rights of the parties (e.g., a change in the paying office or the appropriation data). Effective dates for modifications are defined in subsections (1) through (5).
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_201: Definitions applicable to Part 43 contract modifications including administrative change definition and effective date rules
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for definitions section. Administrative change definition references 43.203(b) for unilateral modifications. Five subsections define effective dates for different modification types.

Natural_Language: Administrative change means a unilateral (see 43.203(b)) contract change, in writing, that does not affect the substantive rights of the parties (e.g., a change in the paying office or the appropriation data).

Validation_Notes: Definitional provision establishing three conjunctive criteria for administrative change: must be unilateral, must be in writing, and must not affect substantive rights. Cross-references 43.203(b) for unilateral modification definition.

Natural_Language: For a solicitation amendment, change order, or administrative change, the effective date shall be the issue date of the amendment, change order, or administrative change.

Validation_Notes: Conditional: if modification type is solicitation amendment, change order, or administrative change, then effective date equals issue date. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15 but straightforward conditional mapping.

Natural_Language: For a supplemental agreement, the effective date shall be the date agreed upon by the contracting parties.

Validation_Notes: Conditional: if modification is supplemental agreement, then effective date is the date agreed by parties. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: For a modification issued as a confirming notice of termination for the convenience of the Government, the effective date of the confirming notice shall be the same as the effective date of the initial notice.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_201_3_a: Modification is a confirming notice of termination for convenience; P_43_201_3_b: Effective date of confirming notice equals effective date of initial notice
Validation_Notes: Conditional tying confirming notice effective date to initial notice effective date. Ensures temporal consistency in termination for convenience actions. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: For a modification converting a termination for default to a termination for the convenience of the Government, the effective date shall be the same as the effective date of the termination for default.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_201_4_a: Modification converts termination for default to termination for convenience; P_43_201_4_b: Effective date equals effective date of the termination for default
Validation_Notes: Conditional linking conversion modification effective date back to original T4D date. Preserves original timeline when converting termination type. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: For a modification confirming the termination contracting officer's previous letter determination of the amount due in settlement of a contract termination for convenience, the effective date shall be the same as the effective date of the previous letter determination.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_201_5_a: Modification confirms TCO previous letter determination of amount due in T4C settlement; P_43_201_5_b: Effective date equals effective date of previous letter determination
Validation_Notes: Conditional tying confirming modification date to prior TCO letter determination date for T4C settlement. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Policy governing contract modifications including authority limitations and pricing requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_202: Contract modification policy requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for policy section covering authority restrictions and pricing policy.

Natural_Language: Only contracting officers acting within the scope of their authority may execute contract modifications on behalf of the Government. Other Government personnel shall not: (1) Execute contract modifications; (2) Act in such a manner as to cause the contractor to believe that they have authority to bind the Government; or (3) Direct or encourage the contractor to perform work that should be the subject of a contract modification.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_202_a_auth: Only contracting officers acting within scope of authority may execute contract modifications on behalf of Government; P_43_202_a_1: Other Government personnel shall not execute contract modifications; P_43_202_a_2: Other Government personnel shall not act to cause contractor to believe they have authority to bind the Government; P_43_202_a_3: Other Government personnel shall not direct or encourage contractor to perform work that should be subject of contract modification
Validation_Notes: Parent for 43.202(a). Establishes exclusive CO authority for contract modifications and three prohibitions on other government personnel. Subsections (1)-(3) are conjunctive prohibitions (all apply simultaneously).

Natural_Language: Other Government personnel shall not execute contract modifications.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_202_a_1: Other Government personnel execute contract modifications
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on non-CO personnel executing contract modifications. Simple negation of the prohibited action.

Natural_Language: Other Government personnel shall not act in such a manner as to cause the contractor to believe that they have authority to bind the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_202_a_2: Other Government personnel act to cause contractor to believe they have authority to bind the Government
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on apparent authority creation. Prevents constructive authorization or implied authority scenarios.

Natural_Language: Other Government personnel shall not direct or encourage the contractor to perform work that should be the subject of a contract modification.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_202_a_3: Other Government personnel direct or encourage contractor to perform work that should be subject of contract modification
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on directing or encouraging unauthorized work. Prevents constructive changes without proper contract modification documentation.

Natural_Language: Contract modifications, including changes that could be issued unilaterally, shall be priced before their execution if this can be done without adversely affecting the interest of the Government. If a significant cost increase could result from a contract modification and time does not permit negotiation of a price, at least a ceiling price shall be negotiated unless impractical.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_202_b_a: Contract modifications shall be priced before execution; P_43_202_b_b: Pricing before execution can be done without adversely affecting Government interest; P_43_202_b_c: Significant cost increase could result from modification; P_43_202_b_d: Time does not permit negotiation of price; P_43_202_b_e: Ceiling price shall be negotiated; P_43_202_b_f: Negotiation of ceiling price is impractical
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Two-part conditional: (1) price before execution if feasible without harming Government interest; (2) if significant cost increase possible and no time for full price negotiation and ceiling negotiation is not impractical, then negotiate ceiling price. Complex nested conditional with exception handling. HIGH-RISK due to multiple Rule 15 applications.

Natural_Language: Contract modifications are of the following types: bilateral and unilateral.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_203: Contract modifications consist of bilateral and unilateral types
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition establishing two types of contract modifications. Exhaustive categorization.

Natural_Language: A bilateral modification (supplemental agreement) is a contract modification that is signed by the contractor and the contracting officer. Bilateral modifications are used to: (1) Make negotiated equitable adjustments resulting from the issuance of a change order; (2) Definitize letter contracts; and (3) Reflect other agreements of the parties modifying the terms of contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_203_a_def: Bilateral modification is signed by contractor and contracting officer; P_43_203_a_1: Bilateral modifications used to make negotiated equitable adjustments from change orders; P_43_203_a_2: Bilateral modifications used to definitize letter contracts; P_43_203_a_3: Bilateral modifications used to reflect other agreements modifying contract terms
Validation_Notes: Definition plus enumerated uses of bilateral modifications. Subsections (1)-(3) are non-exhaustive uses connected by conjunction. Definitional element (both parties sign) is mandatory characteristic.

Natural_Language: A unilateral modification is a contract modification that is signed only by the contracting officer. Unilateral modifications are used, for example, to: (1) Make administrative changes; (2) Issue change orders; (3) Make changes authorized by clauses other than a changes clause (e.g., Property clause, Options clause, or Suspension of Work clause); and (4) Issue termination notices.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_203_b_def: Unilateral modification is signed only by contracting officer; P_43_203_b_1: Unilateral modifications used to make administrative changes; P_43_203_b_2: Unilateral modifications used to issue change orders; P_43_203_b_3: Unilateral modifications used to make changes authorized by clauses other than changes clause; P_43_203_b_4: Unilateral modifications used to issue termination notices
Validation_Notes: Definition plus enumerated uses of unilateral modifications. 'For example' indicates non-exhaustive list. Definitional element (CO-only signature) is mandatory characteristic.

Natural_Language: When a contractor determines that the Government has made or may make a change in the contract that is not in writing and is not signed by the contracting officer, the contractor shall notify the Government in writing as soon as possible. This will permit the Government to evaluate the alleged change and: (a) Confirm that it is a change, direct the mode of further performance, and plan for its funding; (b) Countermand the alleged change; or (c) Notify the contractor that no change is considered to have occurred.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_204_trigger: Contractor determines Government has made or may make a change not in writing and not signed by CO; P_43_204_req: Contractor notifies Government in writing as soon as possible; P_43_204_a: Government confirms change, directs further performance, and plans funding; P_43_204_b: Government countermands alleged change; P_43_204_c: Government notifies contractor no change occurred
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Disjunction (Disj): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Conditional: when contractor identifies potential unwritten/unsigned change, mandatory written notification follows. Government then has three disjunctive response options (a), (b), or (c). The notification requirement is mandatory (shall), and the Government response alternatives are mutually exclusive disjunction. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Availability of funds requirements for contract modifications.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_205: Fund availability requirements for contract modifications
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for fund availability section with three subsections.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer shall not execute a contract modification that causes or will cause an increase in funds without obtaining a certification of fund availability first, except for modifications to contracts that: (1) Are conditioned on availability of funds (see 32.703-2); or (2) Contain a limitation of cost or funds clause (see 32.704).
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_205_a_prohibition: CO shall not execute modification causing fund increase without fund availability certification; P_43_205_a_1: Contract is conditioned on availability of funds; P_43_205_a_2: Contract contains limitation of cost or funds clause
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with two exceptions. If neither exception applies (contract not conditioned on fund availability AND no limitation clause), then fund certification is required before executing modification causing fund increase. External dependencies on Parts 32.703-2 and 32.704. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: The certification required by paragraph (a) of this section shall be based on the negotiated price, except for modifications executed before agreement on price, which may be based on the best available estimate of cost.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_205_b_a: Certification is based on negotiated price; P_43_205_b_b: Modification is executed before agreement on price; P_43_205_b_c: Certification may be based on best available estimate of cost

Validation_Notes: Two conditionals: (1) default rule that certification uses negotiated price; (2) if executed before price agreement, 'may' use estimate (permissive tautology for discretion). Internal dependency on 43.205(a) certification requirement. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 983, do not provide funds by contract or contract modification, or make contract payments, to an institution of higher education that has a policy or practice of hindering Senior Reserve Officer Training Corps units or military recruiting on campus as described at 9.110. The prohibition in this paragraph (c) does not apply to acquisitions at or below the simplified acquisition threshold or to acquisitions of commercial products, including commercially available off-the-shelf items, and commercial services.

Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with two exceptions: if institution hinders SROTC/military recruiting AND acquisition exceeds SAT AND acquisition is not commercial, then funding is prohibited. Statutory basis in 10 U.S.C. 983. External dependency on 9.110 for campus policy description. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may insert a clause substantially the same as the clause at 52.243-7, Notification of Changes, in solicitations and contracts. The clause is available for use primarily in negotiated research and development or supply contracts for the acquisition of major weapon systems or principal subsystems. If the contract amount is expected to be less than $1,000,000, the clause shall not be used, unless the contracting officer anticipates that situations will arise where a contractor alleges that the Government has effected changes other than those identified in writing and signed by the contracting officer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_206_a: CO inserts clause substantially same as 52.243-7 in solicitations and contracts; P_43_206_b: Clause is primarily for negotiated R&D or supply contracts for major weapon systems or principal subsystems; P_43_206_c: Contract amount expected less than $1,000,000; P_43_206_d: CO anticipates contractor will allege Government effected unwritten/unsigned changes
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Complex three-part logic: (1) above $1M, CO has discretion (may = tautology); (2) below $1M without anticipation of change disputes, clause shall not be used; (3) below $1M with anticipation of change disputes, CO regains discretion. Captures the prohibition with exception structure. External dependency on 52.243-7. HIGH-RISK due to multiple Rule 15 applications.

Natural_Language: General provisions governing change orders.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_301: General change order provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for general change order section with three subsections.

Natural_Language: Generally, Government contracts contain a changes clause that permits the contracting officer to make unilateral changes, in designated areas, within the scope of the contract. These are accomplished by issuing written change orders on Standard Form 30, Amendment of Solicitation/Modification of Contract (SF 30), unless otherwise provided (see 43.401).
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_301_a_a: Government contracts contain a changes clause permitting CO unilateral changes within contract scope; P_43_301_a_b: Change orders accomplished by issuing written change orders on SF 30; P_43_301_a_c: Alternative methods otherwise provided
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Establishes default procedure (SF 30) with exception for alternative methods per 43.401. 'Generally' indicates standard practice rather than absolute mandate. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Upon receipt of a change order, the contractor must continue performance of the contract as changed, except for cost-reimbursement or incrementally funded contracts where the contractor is not obligated to continue performance or incur costs beyond the limits established in the Limitation of Cost or Limitation of Funds clause (see 32.706-2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_301_b_a: Contractor receives change order; P_43_301_b_b: Contractor continues performance as changed; P_43_301_b_c: Contract is cost-reimbursement or incrementally funded; P_43_301_b_d: Contractor performance or costs would exceed Limitation of Cost or Limitation of Funds clause limits
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Mandatory performance continuation upon change order receipt, with exception for cost-reimbursement/incrementally funded contracts at funding limits. Exception requires both contract type AND exceeding funding limits. External dependency on 32.706-2. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may issue a change order by electronic means without a SF 30 under unusual or urgent circumstances, provided that the message contains substantially the information required by the SF 30 and immediate action is taken to issue the SF 30.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_301_c_a: Unusual or urgent circumstances exist; P_43_301_c_b: Electronic message contains substantially the information required by SF 30; P_43_301_c_c: Immediate action is taken to issue SF 30; P_43_301_c_d: CO issues change order by electronic means without SF 30
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority (may) for electronic change orders under three conjunctive conditions: unusual/urgent circumstances, substantially complete information, and immediate SF 30 follow-up. Tautological consequent represents CO discretion. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Change orders shall be issued by the contracting officer except when authority is delegated to an administrative contracting officer (see 42.202(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_302_a: Change orders issued by contracting officer; P_43_302_b: Authority is delegated to administrative contracting officer
Validation_Notes: Default rule: CO issues change orders unless authority delegated to ACO. External dependency on 42.202(c) for delegation provisions. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: The following categories of direct costs normally are segregable and accountable under the terms of the Change Order Accounting clause at 52.243-6: (a) Nonrecurring costs; (b) Costs of added distinct work; (c) Costs of recurring work.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_303: Direct cost categories segregable under Change Order Accounting clause
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition identifying three categories of segregable direct costs. External dependency on 52.243-6 clause. 'Normally' indicates standard practice with possible exceptions.

Validation_Notes: Identifies nonrecurring costs as a segregable category. Examples provided are illustrative (such as).

Validation_Notes: Identifies added distinct work costs as a segregable category. Examples illustrative.

Natural_Language: Administration of change orders including documentation, definitization, and equitable adjustments.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_304: Change order administration requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for administration section covering documentation, definitization, and equitable adjustment procedures.

Natural_Language: Documentation of unilaterally issued change orders that are later definitized through a bilateral supplement agreement contract modification requires two documents: the initial SF-30 change order and then the subsequent SF-30 supplemental agreement reflecting the resulting equitable adjustment in contract terms. If an equitable adjustment in the contract price or delivery terms or both can be agreed upon in advance, only a bilateral supplemental agreement contract modification (SF-30) need be issued. Administrative changes and change orders issued pursuant to a clause giving the Government a unilateral right to make a change (e.g., an option clause) require only the unilateral SF-30 change order.
Atomic_Propositions: P_43_304_a_a: Change order is unilaterally issued and later definitized bilaterally; P_43_304_a_b: Two SF-30 documents required (initial change order + supplemental agreement); P_43_304_a_c: Equitable adjustment can be agreed upon in advance; P_43_304_a_d: Only bilateral supplemental agreement SF-30 required; P_43_304_a_e: Change is administrative or pursuant to unilateral right clause; P_43_304_a_f: Only unilateral SF-30 required
Validation_Notes: Three conditional documentation requirements based on modification scenario: (1) unilateral then bilateral = two SF-30s; (2) advance agreement = single bilateral SF-30; (3) administrative/unilateral clause = single unilateral SF-30. Mutually exclusive scenarios. HIGH-RISK due to multiple Rule 15 applications.

Natural_Language: Agencies shall, in accordance with agency procedures, record and maintain data regarding the time required to definitize equitable adjustments associated with change orders for construction. The definitization of an equitable adjustment begins when the contracting officer receives an adequate change order definitization proposal and ends when the contracting officer executes a contractual action to definitize the change order. The contracting officer shall ensure the data is recorded promptly in accordance with agency procedures. See 36.211(b).
